hook.en: Divide every integer by 2 and look at the remainder: the whole of Z splits neatly into evens and odds. Relations that sort a set into such groups are called equivalence relations.
hook.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಪೂರ್ಣಾಂಕವನ್ನು 2 ರಿಂದ ಭಾಗಿಸಿ ಶೇಷ ನೋಡಿ: Z ಸಮ ಮತ್ತು ಬೆಸ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳಾಗಿ ವಿಭಜನೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೀಗೆ ಗುಂಪು ಮಾಡುವ ಸಂಬಂಧಗಳೇ ಸಮಾನತಾ ಸಂಬಂಧಗಳು.

body.en: A relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive is an equivalence relation. Example: on $Z$, $R = \{(a, b) : 2 \text{ divides } a - b\}$ is an equivalence relation.
body.kn: ಸ್ವವಾಚಕ, ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಕ್ರಾಮಕ ಆಗಿರುವ ಸಂಬಂಧವೇ ಸಮಾನತಾ ಸಂಬಂಧ.

points.en: "Is equal to", "is similar to", "has the same remainder as" are equivalence relations
"Is less than" is not (not reflexive, not symmetric)

narration.en: A relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive at the same time is called an equivalence relation.
narration.kn: ಸ್ವವಾಚಕ, ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಕ್ರಾಮಕ ಆಗಿರುವ ಸಂಬಂಧವೇ ಸಮಾನತಾ ಸಂಬಂಧ.

body.en: For an equivalence relation, the equivalence class $[a]$ is the set of all elements related to $a$. Two classes are either equal or disjoint, and together they cover the whole set: they form a partition.
body.kn: a ಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿದ ಎಲ್ಲ ಅಂಶಗಳ ಗಣವೇ ಸಮಾನತಾ ವರ್ಗ [a]. ಎರಡು ವರ್ಗಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಅಥವಾ ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಬೇರ್ಪಟ್ಟಿರುತ್ತವೆ, ಮತ್ತು ಒಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಇಡೀ ಗಣವನ್ನು ಆವರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

narration.en: The equivalence class of a is everything related to a. Different classes never overlap, and together they fill the whole set.

problem.en: Show that R = {(a, b) : |a − b| is even} on A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} is an equivalence relation and find its classes.

steps.en: |a − a| = 0 is even: reflexive. |a − b| = |b − a|: symmetric.
If a − b and b − c are even, a − c = (a − b) + (b − c) is even: transitive.
Elements with the same parity are related: [1] = {1, 3, 5}, [2] = {2, 4}.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Show that R = {(a, b) : |a − b| is even} on A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} is an equivalence relation and find its classes.

problem.en: On Z, R = {(a, b) : 3 divides a − b}. Find [0].

steps.en: a R 0 means 3 divides a − 0, i.e. a is a multiple of 3.
Similarly [1] and [2] give the other two classes.

heading.en: Same-something relations are always equivalence relations

body.en: Any relation of the form "a and b have the same ___" (same remainder, same parity, same length, same age) is automatically reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Comparisons like "less than" or "is a factor of" never are.
